title: Relative rational maps and birational group laws
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X,Y$ schemes over $S$. Products and fibres are scheme-theoretic base changes [def-pc-base-change]. A subset $U\subseteq X$ is $S$-dense when its inverse image in $X_s$ is dense for every $s\in S$. A representative of an $S$-rational map $X\dashrightarrow Y$ consists of an $S$-dense open $D\subseteq X$ and an $S$-morphism $D\to Y$. Two representatives agree when their restrictions to an $S$-dense common open agree; relative rational maps are the quotient by this agreement. Such a map is $S$-birational when it is represented, after restriction, by an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] with $S$-dense image (equivalently, an isomorphism between $S$-dense opens). For a representative $m:X\times_S X\dashrightarrow X$, its universal translations are $(x,y)\mapsto(x,m(x,y))$ and $(x,y)\mapsto(m(x,y),y)$. The representative is associative when $(xy)z=x(yz)$ wherever both composites are defined, as morphisms of schemes, equivalently on points valued in every test $S$-scheme. It is an $S$-birational group law when both universal translations are $S$-birational and it is associative.
